entry_json.avoid: An absolute participle phrase. Follow it with a comma and a full clause.

entry_json.definition: necessarily true because of what the word means
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A measure that counts only reported incidents will by definition miss those never reported.
example_sentences: By definition a part-time job is fewer hours, so of course the pay is lower.
Voluntary schemes attract, by definition, the people already willing to take part.

contexts.text: A measure that counts only reported incidents will by definition miss those never reported.
By definition a part-time job is fewer hours, so of course the pay is lower.
Voluntary schemes attract, by definition, the people already willing to take part.

confusables.difference: Obviously claims the reader should already see it. By definition explains why they must accept it, which is an argument rather than an assertion of the reader's ignorance.
minimal_pair: The sample is by definition self-selecting.
The sample is obviously self-selecting.

entry_json.avoid: No article. It can sit mid-sentence between commas.

entry_json.definition: used to state the minimum that must be accepted or done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: At the very least, the two figures should have been published on the same basis.
example_sentences: At the very least they could have told us it was cancelled.
At the very least, the limitation should be stated in the abstract.

contexts.text: At the very least, the two figures should have been published on the same basis.
At the very least they could have told us it was cancelled.
At the very least, the limitation should be stated in the abstract.

confusables.difference: At least is the plain form and works everywhere. At the very least is emphatic and marks the following claim as the lowest possible bar, which strengthens a criticism.
minimal_pair: At the very least, an explanation was owed.
At least an explanation was given.

entry_json.avoid: Fixed. Not at the least very.

entry_json.definition: used to give one important reason among several
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The comparison is difficult, not least because the two countries count the unemployed differently.
example_sentences: I would not do it again, not least because of what it cost.
The result should be treated cautiously, not least because the follow-up period was short.

contexts.text: The comparison is difficult, not least because the two countries count the unemployed differently.
I would not do it again, not least because of what it cost.
The result should be treated cautiously, not least because the follow-up period was short.

confusables.difference: Because gives the reason. Not least because gives one reason while signalling there are others, which is more accurate when a claim has several supports.
minimal_pair: It failed, not least because nobody was consulted.
It failed because nobody was consulted.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a clause. Not least of all is a wordier variant to avoid.

entry_json.definition: used after a negative to say that a bigger thing is even less likely
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Few households can afford a deposit, let alone the repairs an older property needs.
example_sentences: I cannot get across town in an hour, let alone out to the airport.
The sample could not detect a small effect, let alone a subgroup difference.
collocations: cannot afford X, let alone Y

contexts.text: Few households can afford a deposit, let alone the repairs an older property needs.
I cannot get across town in an hour, let alone out to the airport.
The sample could not detect a small effect, let alone a subgroup difference.

confusables.difference: And also adds an equal item. Let alone adds a larger one and requires a negative before it, so the sentence says even the smaller thing is out of reach.
minimal_pair: She cannot walk to the shop, let alone to the station.
She cannot walk to the shop and also to the station.

entry_json.avoid: Requires a negative in the first clause. The second item must be the harder one.

entry_json.definition: used to add a further consideration that is separate from the one just given
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Quite apart from the cost, the scheme would take longer than the problem allows.
example_sentences: Quite apart from the money, I just did not have the time.
Quite apart from the ethical objection, the design could not answer the question.

chunk.shape: quite apart from X, MAIN CLAUSE

contexts.text: Quite apart from the cost, the scheme would take longer than the problem allows.
Quite apart from the money, I just did not have the time.
Quite apart from the ethical objection, the design could not answer the question.

confusables.difference: Also adds another point of the same kind. Quite apart from marks the new point as belonging to a different category, which reads as a stronger and more organised argument.
minimal_pair: Quite apart from the cost, the timing is wrong.
The cost is high and the timing is also wrong.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun or an -ing form. The main clause must follow.

entry_json.definition: used to limit a claim to the part of the case it actually covers
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The policy succeeded in so far as it reduced waiting, and it did nothing about the cause.
example_sentences: I agree in so far as the cost is a real problem.
The model holds in so far as demand stays within the observed range.
collocations: in so far as it goes

chunk.shape: X is true in so far as Y

contexts.text: The policy succeeded in so far as it reduced waiting, and it did nothing about the cause.
I agree in so far as the cost is a real problem.
The model holds in so far as demand stays within the observed range.

confusables.difference: Because gives a reason. In so far as sets a boundary on how much of the claim you are making, which is a hedge and not a justification.
minimal_pair: It worked in so far as costs fell.
It worked because costs fell.

entry_json.avoid: British writing also spells it insofar as. Be consistent within one piece.

entry_json.definition: in addition to something already counted
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Maintenance costs fall due over and above the price of building the thing in the first place.
example_sentences: That is over and above what we had already agreed.
The intervention added a measurable benefit over and above the standard programme.

contexts.text: Maintenance costs fall due over and above the price of building the thing in the first place.
That is over and above what we had already agreed.
The intervention added a measurable benefit over and above the standard programme.

confusables.difference: As well as simply adds a second item. Over and above stresses that the second is on top of a total already stated, which matters when you are describing costs or effects.
minimal_pair: The fee is charged over and above the deposit.
The fee is charged as well as the deposit.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun phrase. Do not use it as a plain synonym for above.

entry_json.definition: following the same people over a long period of time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Only a longitudinal design can show whether the early advantage lasts into adult life.
example_sentences: It was a longitudinal study, so they followed the same children for twenty years.
Longitudinal data revealed a divergence that the annual snapshots had concealed.

contexts.text: Only a longitudinal design can show whether the early advantage lasts into adult life.
It was a longitudinal study, so they followed the same children for twenty years.
Longitudinal data revealed a divergence that the annual snapshots had concealed.

confusables.difference: A cross-sectional study measures many people once. A longitudinal study measures the same people repeatedly, which is what allows claims about change over time.
minimal_pair: The longitudinal study followed one cohort for thirty years.
The cross-sectional survey measured all ages in one month.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive. It describes the design, not the finding.

entry_json.definition: a group of people who share a starting point and are followed together
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The cohort that entered the labour market in a downturn earned less for a decade afterwards.
example_sentences: My cohort at university was the first to pay the higher fees.
Each cohort was tracked for five years from the point of entry.

contexts.text: The cohort that entered the labour market in a downturn earned less for a decade afterwards.
My cohort at university was the first to pay the higher fees.
Each cohort was tracked for five years from the point of entry.

confusables.difference: A sample is whoever was selected for a study. A cohort is a group defined by sharing a starting event, such as a year of birth or entry.
minimal_pair: The cohort was everyone who started in 2008.
The sample was four hundred drawn at random.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. A cohort study follows one cohort over time.

entry_json.definition: the measurement taken before anything changes, used to judge everything after
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Without a baseline there is no way to know whether the intervention did anything at all.
example_sentences: We took a baseline reading first so we could compare later.
Baseline characteristics were balanced between the two groups.

contexts.text: Without a baseline there is no way to know whether the intervention did anything at all.
We took a baseline reading first so we could compare later.
Baseline characteristics were balanced between the two groups.

confusables.difference: A benchmark is an external standard you compare against. A baseline is your own starting measurement of the same thing, taken before the change.
minimal_pair: The baseline was recorded in January.
The benchmark was the national average.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. At baseline is the fixed phrase in research writing.

entry_json.definition: how common something is in a population at a given moment
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Prevalence rose while the number of new cases each year fell, because people were living longer with it.
example_sentences: The prevalence of that kind of contract has really increased.
Prevalence was estimated from a household survey rather than from clinical records.

contexts.text: Prevalence rose while the number of new cases each year fell, because people were living longer with it.
The prevalence of that kind of contract has really increased.
Prevalence was estimated from a household survey rather than from clinical records.

confusables.difference: Incidence counts new cases arising in a period. Prevalence counts all existing cases at a moment. If people live longer with a condition, prevalence can rise while incidence falls.
minimal_pair: Prevalence was one in twelve adults.
Incidence was four hundred new cases a year.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable. Prevalence of something, never prevalence in.

entry_json.definition: happening in small steps rather than in one large change
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Incremental improvement is the only kind that survives a change of government.
example_sentences: It was all very incremental, you would not notice it month to month.
Incremental gains accumulated to a substantial difference over the full period.

contexts.text: Incremental improvement is the only kind that survives a change of government.
It was all very incremental, you would not notice it month to month.
Incremental gains accumulated to a substantial difference over the full period.

confusables.difference: Gradual describes a smooth continuous change. Incremental describes a change that happens in distinct steps, each one added to the last.
minimal_pair: Incremental changes were made at each annual review.
The gradual warming continued through the spring.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive. Do not use it as a synonym for small.

entry_json.definition: done first and likely to be revised once more work is complete
entry_json.own_context_sentence: These are preliminary figures and the final ones have historically been lower.
example_sentences: The preliminary results looked promising, which is not the same as promising.
Preliminary analysis indicated a difference that did not survive adjustment.

contexts.text: These are preliminary figures and the final ones have historically been lower.
The preliminary results looked promising, which is not the same as promising.
Preliminary analysis indicated a difference that did not survive adjustment.

confusables.difference: Initial simply means first in time. Preliminary adds that the result is provisional and may change, which is a warning as well as a description.
minimal_pair: The preliminary estimate was later revised down.
The initial meeting was held in March.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive. Always signals that a firmer version is coming.

entry_json.definition: offered cautiously and open to being withdrawn
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The authors draw a tentative conclusion and are careful not to build anything on it.
example_sentences: We have a tentative date, but nothing is booked yet.
Only tentative support for the mechanism emerged from the pilot.

word_family.note: in a cautious and provisional way

contexts.text: The authors draw a tentative conclusion and are careful not to build anything on it.
We have a tentative date, but nothing is booked yet.
Only tentative support for the mechanism emerged from the pilot.

confusables.difference: Weak says the evidence is poor. Tentative says the claim is being made cautiously, which may be the right response to good but limited evidence.
minimal_pair: The conclusion is tentative but not weak.
The evidence is weak and the conclusion overstated.

entry_json.avoid: Of conclusions and arrangements. It describes the claim, not the evidence.

entry_json.definition: matching something else in size or seriousness
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The response was not commensurate with the scale of the failure it was meant to address.
example_sentences: The pay was not commensurate with the hours, put it that way.
Funding was commensurate with the number of pupils rather than with need.

contexts.text: The response was not commensurate with the scale of the failure it was meant to address.
The pay was not commensurate with the hours, put it that way.
Funding was commensurate with the number of pupils rather than with need.

confusables.difference: Equal to means exactly the same amount. Commensurate with means proportionate and appropriate, which is a judgement about fit rather than a measurement.
minimal_pair: The penalty was commensurate with the harm.
The penalty was equal to the profit made.

entry_json.avoid: Always with. Formal, so use it once.

entry_json.definition: happening at the same time as something else and connected to it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Longer lives bring a concomitant rise in the years spent in poor health.
example_sentences: There was a concomitant drop in the number of people cycling.
The expansion produced a concomitant increase in maintenance liability.

word_family.note: at the same time and connectedly

contexts.text: Longer lives bring a concomitant rise in the years spent in poor health.
There was a concomitant drop in the number of people cycling.
The expansion produced a concomitant increase in maintenance liability.

confusables.difference: Simultaneous only says two things happened at once. Concomitant adds that they are connected, so one accompanies the other for a reason.
minimal_pair: Growth brought a concomitant rise in costs.
The two announcements were simultaneous.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive and very formal. Accompanying is the plainer alternative.

entry_json.definition: the combining of several separate findings into one coherent account
entry_json.own_context_sentence: What the field needs is a synthesis rather than another study of the same size.
example_sentences: The essay is basically a synthesis of about eight papers.
The synthesis identified two mechanisms that no single study had isolated.

word_family.note: to combine into a coherent whole

contexts.text: What the field needs is a synthesis rather than another study of the same size.
The essay is basically a synthesis of about eight papers.
The synthesis identified two mechanisms that no single study had isolated.

confusables.difference: A summary shortens material without adding anything. A synthesis combines it so that something new emerges from the combination.
minimal_pair: The synthesis produced a conclusion no single paper had reached.
The summary condensed each chapter into a paragraph.

entry_json.avoid: The plural is syntheses. Synthesis of things, not synthesis between.

entry_json.definition: a system of classifying things into types according to shared features
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The paper proposes a typology of four settlement patterns and applies it to sixty towns.
example_sentences: They came up with a whole typology of different customer types.
The typology was derived from the data rather than imposed in advance.

contexts.text: The paper proposes a typology of four settlement patterns and applies it to sixty towns.
They came up with a whole typology of different customer types.
The typology was derived from the data rather than imposed in advance.

confusables.difference: A list names items in no particular relationship. A typology sorts them into types on a stated principle, so each item has exactly one place.
minimal_pair: The typology sorts every case into one of four types.
The list names the twelve sites in alphabetical order.

entry_json.avoid: A typology of something. Countable.

entry_json.definition: the view that is currently accepted as correct by most people in a field
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The orthodoxy of one decade is often the discarded assumption of the next.
example_sentences: It went against the orthodoxy at the time and turned out to be right.
The prevailing orthodoxy was challenged by evidence from two independent groups.

contexts.text: The orthodoxy of one decade is often the discarded assumption of the next.
It went against the orthodoxy at the time and turned out to be right.
The prevailing orthodoxy was challenged by evidence from two independent groups.

confusables.difference: A consensus is agreement reached from evidence and can be revised. An orthodoxy is agreement that has hardened into a default, and the word carries a hint of criticism.
minimal_pair: The orthodoxy went unquestioned for twenty years.
The consensus emerged from thirty trials.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Usually with the. Slightly critical in tone.

entry_json.definition: the force or event that gets a change moving
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The court ruling gave impetus to reforms that had stalled for years.
example_sentences: The impetus came from the residents rather than from the council.
Fresh impetus followed the publication of the independent review.

contexts.text: The court ruling gave impetus to reforms that had stalled for years.
The impetus came from the residents rather than from the council.
Fresh impetus followed the publication of the independent review.

confusables.difference: Motivation is internal and belongs to a person. Impetus is external and belongs to a situation, so an event provides impetus rather than feeling it.
minimal_pair: The report gave impetus to the campaign.
Her motivation was personal experience.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable. Give impetus to something, or provide the impetus for it.

entry_json.definition: a system in which things are ranked one above another
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The evidence hierarchy places trials above observation, which is right more often than always.
example_sentences: There is a strict hierarchy in that organisation and everyone knows their place.
A hierarchy of needs was used to prioritise the interventions.
collocations: at the top of the hierarchy

contexts.text: The evidence hierarchy places trials above observation, which is right more often than always.
There is a strict hierarchy in that organisation and everyone knows their place.
A hierarchy of needs was used to prioritise the interventions.

confusables.difference: Order is any sequence, including alphabetical. A hierarchy ranks by importance or authority, and the higher levels control or outrank the lower.
minimal_pair: The hierarchy puts randomised trials at the top.
The order was chronological.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. A hierarchy of things. Note the spelling with ie.

entry_json.definition: similar in a way that makes a comparison useful
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The problem is analogous to congestion, in that adding capacity increases demand.
example_sentences: It is analogous to a queue, really, everyone waiting for the same thing.
The mechanism is analogous to one described in an unrelated field.

contexts.text: The problem is analogous to congestion, in that adding capacity increases demand.
It is analogous to a queue, really, everyone waiting for the same thing.
The mechanism is analogous to one described in an unrelated field.

confusables.difference: Similar to says two things resemble each other. Analogous to says the resemblance is structural and lets you carry reasoning from one to the other, which is a stronger claim.
minimal_pair: The situation is analogous to a bank run.
The building is similar to the one next door.

entry_json.avoid: Always to, never with. The noun is analogy.

entry_json.definition: used to describe an impression that closer examination will overturn
entry_json.own_context_sentence: At first sight the two datasets agree, though they cover different age ranges.
example_sentences: At first sight it looked like a bargain.
At first sight, the fall appears sudden, but the series is monthly rather than annual.

contexts.text: At first sight the two datasets agree, though they cover different age ranges.
At first sight it looked like a bargain.
At first sight, the fall appears sudden, but the series is monthly rather than annual.

confusables.difference: Obviously claims something is clear and true. At first sight says it only looks that way and warns the reader that a correction is coming.
minimal_pair: At first sight the trend is upward.
Obviously the trend is upward.

entry_json.avoid: Follow it with the correction. Alone it leaves a promise unkept.

entry_json.definition: used to give one sufficient reason even if others are debatable
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The scheme deserves attention if only because nothing else has been tried in thirty years.
example_sentences: I would go back, if only because the food was so good.
The measure should be reported, if only because readers will otherwise assume it was omitted.

contexts.text: The scheme deserves attention if only because nothing else has been tried in thirty years.
I would go back, if only because the food was so good.
The measure should be reported, if only because readers will otherwise assume it was omitted.

confusables.difference: Because gives the reason. If only because gives a reason that is enough on its own, conceding that the other reasons may be arguable, which is a confident and economical move.
minimal_pair: It is worth doing, if only because it is cheap.
It is worth doing because it is cheap.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a clause. If only to plus an infinitive is the parallel form.

entry_json.definition: an example that illustrates exactly the argument being made
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The northern line extension is a case in point, since it created demand it then could not carry.
example_sentences: My old school is a case in point, they closed the library first.
The second trial is a case in point, having been stopped for the reason predicted.

chunk.shape: X is a case in point

contexts.text: The northern line extension is a case in point, since it created demand it then could not carry.
My old school is a case in point, they closed the library first.
The second trial is a case in point, having been stopped for the reason predicted.

confusables.difference: An example illustrates a general statement. A case in point illustrates the specific argument you are making right now, which is a tighter and more purposeful use.
minimal_pair: The closure is a case in point.
The closure is an example of a wider trend.

entry_json.avoid: Keep the article. The example must actually fit the argument, or it undermines it.

entry_json.definition: used to say a finding is interesting enough to justify more work
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The pattern in the second cohort warrants further investigation before any policy is built on it.
example_sentences: It is odd enough that it warrants further investigation, I would say.
The unexplained variation warrants further investigation using a longitudinal design.

contexts.text: The pattern in the second cohort warrants further investigation before any policy is built on it.
It is odd enough that it warrants further investigation, I would say.
The unexplained variation warrants further investigation using a longitudinal design.

confusables.difference: We need more research is a filler sentence that appears at the end of everything. Warrants further investigation attaches the claim to a specific finding, which makes it mean something.
minimal_pair: The anomaly warrants further investigation.
More research is needed.

entry_json.avoid: The subject must be singular for warrants. Name what warrants it.

entry_json.definition: used to state a condition a calculation or argument depends on
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The forecast is built on the assumption that the population continues to grow at the current rate.
example_sentences: We booked it on the assumption that the flights would be refundable.
Costs were projected on the assumption that the pilot scales linearly.

contexts.text: The forecast is built on the assumption that the population continues to grow at the current rate.
We booked it on the assumption that the flights would be refundable.
Costs were projected on the assumption that the pilot scales linearly.

confusables.difference: If is a plain conditional and can be about any possibility. On the assumption that names something you have deliberately taken as given, which is a stronger admission and easier to challenge honestly.
minimal_pair: The model runs on the assumption that demand is fixed.
If demand is fixed, the model works.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a full clause. State the assumption you are actually making.

entry_json.definition: used to say two things are far less alike than someone has claimed
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The scheme as delivered bears little resemblance to the one that was consulted on.
example_sentences: The photo bears little resemblance to the actual room.
The replicated protocol bears little resemblance to the original in three respects.

chunk.shape: X bears little resemblance to Y

contexts.text: The scheme as delivered bears little resemblance to the one that was consulted on.
The photo bears little resemblance to the actual room.
The replicated protocol bears little resemblance to the original in three respects.

confusables.difference: Is different from states a difference. Bears little resemblance to says the two were presented as the same and are not, which is a criticism rather than a description.
minimal_pair: The final scheme bears little resemblance to the plan.
The final scheme is different from the plan.

entry_json.avoid: Resemblance to, never resemblance with. Bears agrees with a singular subject.

entry_json.definition: used to say what happens or what must be assumed when something is missing
entry_json.own_context_sentence: In the absence of a control group, the improvement cannot be separated from what would have happened anyway.
example_sentences: In the absence of any timetable, people just turn up and hope.
In the absence of direct measurement, the value was estimated from a proxy.
collocations: in the absence of any alternative

chunk.shape: in the absence of X, CLAUSE

contexts.text: In the absence of a control group, the improvement cannot be separated from what would have happened anyway.
In the absence of any timetable, people just turn up and hope.
In the absence of direct measurement, the value was estimated from a proxy.

confusables.difference: Without is plain and works everywhere. In the absence of is formal and draws attention to the gap itself, which suits an argument about what the evidence cannot show.
minimal_pair: In the absence of data, we can only speculate.
Without data, we can only speculate.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun phrase. Keep the article before absence.

entry_json.definition: used to say a gain was achieved by giving up something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Faster processing came at the expense of the checks that had caught the errors.
example_sentences: The extra hours came at the expense of seeing anyone at the weekend.
Higher yields come at the expense of soil structure that takes decades to rebuild.
collocations: must not come at the expense of

chunk.shape: X comes at the expense of Y

contexts.text: Faster processing came at the expense of the checks that had caught the errors.
The extra hours came at the expense of seeing anyone at the weekend.
Higher yields come at the expense of soil structure that takes decades to rebuild.

confusables.difference: Replace says one thing took the other's place. Come at the expense of says the first was gained by sacrificing the second, which names a cost rather than a swap.
minimal_pair: Speed came at the expense of accuracy.
The new system replaced the old one.

entry_json.avoid: Always the expense. Not at expense of.

contexts.gap_span: There is a strong case for

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun or an -ing form. Not by an infinitive.

entry_json.definition: needed for a particular purpose
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The department lacked the requisite expertise to assess the tender it had written.
example_sentences: I did not have the requisite paperwork, so I had to go back.
Participants without the requisite baseline data were excluded.

contexts.text: The department lacked the requisite expertise to assess the tender it had written.
I did not have the requisite paperwork, so I had to go back.
Participants without the requisite baseline data were excluded.

confusables.difference: Necessary is the everyday word and works in any sentence. Requisite is formal, attributive and usually appears with skills, experience or approval.
minimal_pair: She lacked the requisite qualifications.
It is necessary to apply in writing.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive only. Do not write the qualifications are requisite.

entry_json.definition: used when making something shorter or more impressive has made it harder to understand
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The summary was compressed at the expense of clarity, and readers drew the opposite conclusion.
example_sentences: He shortened it at the expense of clarity, nobody knew what he meant.
Notation was simplified at the expense of clarity in two of the derivations.

chunk.shape: X was done at the expense of clarity

contexts.text: The summary was compressed at the expense of clarity, and readers drew the opposite conclusion.
He shortened it at the expense of clarity, nobody knew what he meant.
Notation was simplified at the expense of clarity in two of the derivations.

confusables.difference: Badly written is a general judgement. At the expense of clarity names the trade that was made, which is more precise and can be acted on.
minimal_pair: The passage was cut at the expense of clarity.
The passage was badly written.

entry_json.avoid: Names a trade-off, so say what was gained as well as what was lost.

entry_json.definition: used before a comparison that shows the true size of a figure
entry_json.own_context_sentence: To put it in perspective, that is roughly what the same authority spends on grass cutting.
example_sentences: To put it in perspective, I spend more on coffee than on that.
To put it in perspective, the effect is smaller than the seasonal variation.

chunk.shape: to put it in perspective, CLAUSE

contexts.text: To put it in perspective, that is roughly what the same authority spends on grass cutting.
To put it in perspective, I spend more on coffee than on that.
To put it in perspective, the effect is smaller than the seasonal variation.

confusables.difference: In fact introduces a correction. To put it in perspective introduces a comparison that makes a number meaningful, which is a more useful move when quoting figures.
minimal_pair: To put it in perspective, that is one day of the budget.
In fact, the budget is much larger.

entry_json.avoid: Follow it with a concrete comparison, not with another bare figure.

entry_json.definition: used to pick out the most significant example from a group
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Several regions improved, notably the two that had received the additional funding.

We stayed in a hostel and met about half the people we still know.
Hostel capacity grew fastest in the cities with the largest student populations.

confusables.difference: A hotel gives each party a private room with its own facilities. A hostel usually means a shared room and shared bathroom, which is why it costs a fraction as much.
minimal_pair: The hostel dormitory slept eight.
The hotel room had its own bathroom.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Stay in a hostel, not at one, in British usage.

entry_json.definition: official guidance about the risks of visiting a particular place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A travel advisory affects insurance long before it affects whether anybody actually goes.
example_sentences: There was a travel advisory out, so the trip got cancelled.
Travel advisory changes preceded the fall in bookings by about three weeks.

contexts.text: A travel advisory affects insurance long before it affects whether anybody actually goes.
There was a travel advisory out, so the trip got cancelled.
Travel advisory changes preceded the fall in bookings by about three weeks.

confusables.difference: A travel ban forbids the journey. A travel advisory only warns, and going anyway is legal though it may void your insurance.
minimal_pair: The travel advisory recommended against non-essential travel.
The travel ban closed the border entirely.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Issue or lift an advisory. Advisory with an s in the plural becomes advisories.

entry_json.definition: a particular way of expressing something that is distinctive or memorable
entry_json.own_context_sentence: One careless turn of phrase can undo a paragraph of careful qualification.
example_sentences: He has a lovely turn of phrase, you remember what he says.
A single turn of phrase in the summary was quoted more than the findings themselves.

contexts.text: One careless turn of phrase can undo a paragraph of careful qualification.
He has a lovely turn of phrase, you remember what he says.
A single turn of phrase in the summary was quoted more than the findings themselves.

confusables.difference: An expression is any fixed phrase people use. A turn of phrase is the individual writer's way of putting something, and it may be entirely original.
minimal_pair: Her turn of phrase made the point land.
The expression dates from the nineteenth century.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Of phrase, singular, never of phrases.

entry_json.definition: an arrangement letting a company take a varying amount from your account each month
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A direct debit transfers the decision about how much to take from you to the supplier.
example_sentences: Everything goes out by direct debit on the first of the month.
Households paying by direct debit were charged a lower unit rate.

contexts.text: A direct debit transfers the decision about how much to take from you to the supplier.
Everything goes out by direct debit on the first of the month.
Households paying by direct debit were charged a lower unit rate.

confusables.difference: A standing order is a fixed sum you control. A direct debit lets the company vary the amount, which matters when prices change.
minimal_pair: The energy supplier varies the direct debit twice a year.
The standing order stays at fifty pounds whatever happens.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Pay by direct debit, not with one.

entry_json.definition: how hard the body is working during an activity
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Recording the level of exertion a participant reports is cheaper than measuring it and nearly as useful.
example_sentences: You should be able to talk at that level of exertion, that is the test.
Level of exertion was self-reported on a standard scale after each session.

word_family.note: to apply physical or mental effort

contexts.text: Recording the level of exertion a participant reports is cheaper than measuring it and nearly as useful.
You should be able to talk at that level of exertion, that is the test.
Level of exertion was self-reported on a standard scale after each session.

confusables.difference: Fitness is a lasting capacity of the body. Level of exertion is how hard you are working right now, and the same effort feels different at different fitness levels.
minimal_pair: The level of exertion was moderate throughout.
Her fitness improved over eight weeks.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable. Perceived exertion is the standard research term.

entry_json.definition: a drink or bar sold as a substitute for a normal meal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A meal replacement solves the calorie question and leaves every other question open.
example_sentences: I tried a meal replacement thing for a month and hated it.
Meal replacement use was recorded alongside conventional dietary intake.

word_family.note: to take the place of something

contexts.text: A meal replacement solves the calorie question and leaves every other question open.
I tried a meal replacement thing for a month and hated it.
Meal replacement use was recorded alongside conventional dietary intake.

confusables.difference: A supplement is taken in addition to food. A meal replacement is taken instead of it, so the two do opposite things.
minimal_pair: The meal replacement was taken instead of lunch.
The supplement was taken alongside meals.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Not the same as a dietary supplement.

entry_json.definition: to recover quickly after a setback or defeat
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Sides that bounce back from a heavy defeat usually do so because nothing was said about it that week.
example_sentences: She bounce back from the injury much faster than anyone expected.
Participants who bounce back from an early failure completed the programme at a higher rate.

contexts.text: Sides that bounce back from a heavy defeat usually do so because nothing was said about it that week.
She bounce back from the injury much faster than anyone expected.
Participants who bounce back from an early failure completed the programme at a higher rate.

confusables.difference: Recover is neutral about speed and works for anything including an economy. Bounce back from is informal and implies the return was fast and complete.
minimal_pair: She bounced back from the injury in six weeks.
The patient recovered slowly over two years.

entry_json.avoid: Three parts. Bounce back from a setback, not bounce back of.

entry_json.definition: to reduce the size or amount of something deliberately
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Households scale back fresh food before they touch anything that is already paid for monthly.
example_sentences: I have scale back takeaways since the prices went up.
Respondents scale back discretionary categories before essential ones.

contexts.text: Households scale back fresh food before they touch anything that is already paid for monthly.
I have scale back takeaways since the prices went up.
Respondents scale back discretionary categories before essential ones.

confusables.difference: Scale back means keeping the thing and making it smaller. Cut out means stopping it entirely, so the two describe very different decisions.
minimal_pair: They scaled back the programme to two sites.
They cut the programme entirely.

entry_json.avoid: Separable. Scale it back or scale back the plan, both work.

entry_json.definition: the strain that large numbers of visitors put on a place and its residents
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Visitor pressure is concentrated in six weeks and paid for across the whole year.
example_sentences: The visitor pressure in August is unbearable for anyone who lives here.
Visitor pressure was measured as arrivals per resident per week.

contexts.text: Visitor pressure is concentrated in six weeks and paid for across the whole year.
The visitor pressure in August is unbearable for anyone who lives here.
Visitor pressure was measured as arrivals per resident per week.

confusables.difference: Demand is how many people want to come and is a market measure. Visitor pressure is what their arrival does to the place, which is an impact measure.
minimal_pair: Visitor pressure eroded the footpaths.
Demand exceeded the number of tickets available.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable. Pressure on a place, not pressure of.

entry_json.definition: generally true when everything is taken together
entry_json.own_context_sentence: On the whole the reform achieved what it set out to do, at a cost nobody had costed.
example_sentences: On the whole I would say it was worth it.
On the whole, the two methods produced comparable estimates.

contexts.text: On the whole the reform achieved what it set out to do, at a cost nobody had costed.
On the whole I would say it was worth it.
On the whole, the two methods produced comparable estimates.

confusables.difference: Completely allows no exceptions. On the whole explicitly allows them and states the overall direction, which is safer and more accurate for a summary judgement.
minimal_pair: On the whole the scheme succeeded.
The scheme completely succeeded.

entry_json.avoid: Keep the article. Not on whole.

entry_json.definition: to work something out from basic truths rather than from what is usually done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Anyone redesigning the curriculum should start from first principles rather than from the current timetable.
example_sentences: I had to start from first principles because none of the guides matched our setup.
The team chose to start from first principles instead of adapting the existing model.

chunk.shape: start from first principles on X

contexts.text: Anyone redesigning the curriculum should start from first principles rather than from the current timetable.
I had to start from first principles because none of the guides matched our setup.
The team chose to start from first principles instead of adapting the existing model.

confusables.difference: Start from scratch means building again with no existing material. Start from first principles means reasoning again from basic truths, and you may end up keeping most of what exists.
minimal_pair: They reasoned from first principles and kept two thirds of the old design.
They started from scratch with an empty page.

entry_json.avoid: Plural principles. Not from a first principle.

entry_json.definition: the fact that you can do something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Reading quickly is a useful ability in the IELTS test.
example_sentences: She has the ability to explain hard ideas in simple words.
Children lose the ability to hear new sounds very early.

confusables.difference: An ability is what you are able to do, often something you were born with. A skill is something you learned and practised, like driving or cooking.

entry_json.avoid: Say "the ability to speak", not "the ability of speaking".

entry_json.definition: having what you need in order to do something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was able to finish the essay before the time ran out.
example_sentences: Are you able to come to class on Friday?
Not everyone is able to study and work at the same time.

confusables.difference: They mean the same, but 'can' has no future or perfect form. Use 'will be able to' and 'have been able to' where 'can' will not work.

entry_json.avoid: After 'able' use 'to' and a verb: "able to swim", never "able swim".

entry_json.definition: on the subject of; or a little more or less than a number
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The talk was about how cities can cut traffic.
example_sentences: We spoke about my plans for next year.
It takes about twenty minutes to walk there.

contexts.text: Tell me about the town where you grew up.
The report is about the cost of public transport.

entry_json.definition: higher than something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The temperature stayed above thirty degrees all week.
example_sentences: My flat is above a small coffee shop.
Scores above seven are treated as strong.

confusables.difference: 'Above' means higher in position or in number, with no touching and no movement. 'Over' can also mean covering or crossing: a bridge goes over a river, not above it.

entry_json.definition: in or to another country
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Studying abroad taught me more than any course at home.
example_sentences: My sister works abroad and sends money to my parents.
Have you ever travelled abroad on your own?
entry_json.avoid: Never "go to abroad" or "in abroad". Abroad already contains the idea of 'to' and 'in'.

entry_json.definition: to say yes to something that is offered, or to agree that something is true
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I accepted the job because the hours suited my studies.
example_sentences: The university accepted her application in March.
Most people now accept that the climate is changing.

confusables.difference: These sound close but do different work. Accept is a verb: I accept your offer. Except means 'not including': everyone except me.

entry_json.definition: something bad that happens without anyone planning it, often hurting someone
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There was a road accident near the school, so the bus was late.
example_sentences: He broke his arm in a cycling accident.
Better street lighting would prevent many accidents.
entry_json.avoid: We have an accident; we do not 'do' or 'make' an accident.

entry_json.definition: to succeed in doing something after trying hard
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I achieved the band score I needed on my second attempt.
example_sentences: She achieved excellent results in her final exams.
Nothing is achieved without regular practice.

confusables.difference: You reach a place or a level; you achieve a goal or a result. 'Reach my goal' is possible, but 'achieve' is the stronger word in writing.

entry_json.definition: from one side of something to the other side
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We walked across the bridge to reach the old town.
example_sentences: There is a chemist across the road from my house.
The disease spread quickly across the country.

confusables.difference: Across is over a flat surface, like a road or a field. Through is inside something with sides or a roof, like a tunnel, a forest or a crowd.

entry_json.definition: to do something, especially to deal with a problem; also to play a part in a play or film
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Governments need to act now if they want to cut pollution.
example_sentences: The police acted quickly and nobody was hurt.
She has acted in three films this year.

entry_json.definition: the process of doing something in order to change a situation
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Talking about waste is easy; taking action is harder.
example_sentences: The council took action after the flood.
Urgent action is needed to protect the forest.
entry_json.avoid: We TAKE action. Never "do action" or "make action".

entry_json.definition: busy doing things, especially moving your body
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Cycling to work keeps me active during the week.
example_sentences: My grandmother is still very active at eighty.
He is an active member of the local sports club.

entry_json.definition: something that you do, often for fun or for a purpose
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Swimming is my favourite weekend activity.
example_sentences: The school offers a range of after-school activities.
Outdoor activities are popular with young families.

entry_json.definition: a person whose job is to play a part in a film, play or television programme
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My favourite actor started out in small theatre roles.
example_sentences: The actor spoke about the training the part required.
Very few actors earn a lot of money.

entry_json.definition: a woman whose job is to play a part in a film, play or television programme
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The actress who played the mother was only twenty-five.
example_sentences: She became a well-known actress in her thirties.
The award for best actress went to a newcomer.

confusables.difference: Many women now prefer 'actor' for both men and women. 'Actress' is still correct and common, but 'actor' is the safer neutral choice.

entry_json.definition: used to say what is really true, often when it is different from what people think
entry_json.own_context_sentence: People say the course is hard, but actually the first year is quite gentle.
example_sentences: I thought it was expensive, but it was actually quite cheap.
Actually, I have never been to the capital.

confusables.difference: In many languages the word that looks like 'actually' means 'now'. In English it does not. For 'now', say currently or at the moment.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use 'actually' to mean 'at present'. "I actually live in Rome" means "in fact I live in Rome", not "I live there now".

entry_json.definition: to put something with something else to make it bigger or more complete
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I added a short conclusion to make the essay complete.
example_sentences: Add a little salt to the water before it boils.
The new line will add ten stations to the network.

entry_json.definition: a person who has finished growing and is no longer a child
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The class is for adults who work during the day.
example_sentences: Adults pay full price; children under ten go free.
Many adults return to study in their thirties.

entry_json.definition: something that helps you or puts you in a better position
entry_json.own_context_sentence: One advantage of living near campus is that I save on travel.
example_sentences: Speaking two languages is a real advantage at work.
The essay asks for the advantages and disadvantages of online study.

confusables.difference: An advantage is a better position, usually compared with someone or something else. A benefit is a good result that you receive, like better health.

entry_json.avoid: Say "an advantage of doing something" or "the advantage is that...", not "the advantage to do".

entry_json.definition: an exciting experience, often one that could be dangerous
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Travelling alone for the first time felt like a real adventure.
example_sentences: The trip turned into an adventure when the road was closed.
Children need a sense of adventure, not just screens.

entry_json.definition: to tell the public about a product or job so that people will buy it or apply
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The company advertises its courses on social media.
example_sentences: The job was advertised in the local paper.
Firms should not be allowed to advertise junk food to children.

entry_json.definition: a notice, picture or short film that tries to make people buy something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I found my flat through an advertisement on a student website.
example_sentences: There was a full-page advertisement in the newspaper.
Children see hundreds of advertisements every week.

confusables.difference: An advertisement is one single notice or film. Advertising is the whole business or activity, and cannot be counted: "advertising is expensive", but "three advertisements".

entry_json.avoid: In speech people usually say 'advert' or 'ad'. Note the British stress: ad-VER-tis-ment.

entry_json.definition: the business of telling the public about products so that they buy them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Advertising aimed at young children should be limited.
example_sentences: She works in advertising for a small agency.
Online advertising now earns more than television.
entry_json.avoid: Advertising is uncountable. Not "an advertising" or "advertisings".

entry_json.definition: words that tell someone what you think they should do
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My teacher gave me some useful advice about timing the writing task.
example_sentences: Can I ask you for some advice?
The website offers free advice on student visas.

confusables.difference: Advice is the noun and ends in a soft 'ss' sound. Advise is the verb and ends in a 'z' sound: she advised me to wait, and it was good advice.

entry_json.avoid: Advice is uncountable. Not "an advice" or "advices" — say "a piece of advice".

entry_json.definition: to make something change, usually in a way you did not choose
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Noise from the road affects my sleep during the week.
example_sentences: The strike affected thousands of passengers.
Long working hours affect family life.

confusables.difference: Affect is the verb, effect is the noun. Pollution affects health; pollution has an effect on health. If you can put 'the' in front of it, you need effect.

entry_json.avoid: Not "affect to" or "affect on". The verb takes a direct object: it affects health.

entry_json.definition: feeling fear; worried that something bad may happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was afraid of speaking English in public until I joined a club.
example_sentences: She is afraid of flying, so she takes the train.
I am afraid I cannot come on Saturday.
entry_json.avoid: 'I'm afraid...' is a polite way to give bad news, and has nothing to do with fear.

entry_json.definition: later than something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: After the exam I slept for twelve hours.
example_sentences: I usually study after dinner.
She went back to work after two months.

confusables.difference: After needs something to follow it: after lunch. Afterwards stands alone at the end: we had lunch and went shopping afterwards.

entry_json.avoid: After a time expression use the present for the future: "After I finish, I will call you", not "After I will finish".

entry_json.definition: the part of the day between midday and the evening
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I have lectures every Tuesday afternoon.
example_sentences: Shall we meet on Friday afternoon?
The shop closes at two in the afternoon.
entry_json.avoid: Use 'in the afternoon' generally, but 'on Monday afternoon' for a named day.

entry_json.definition: one more time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I read the question again to make sure I had understood it.
example_sentences: Could you say that again, please?
He failed the test but sat it again in June.

entry_json.definition: not agreeing with something, or opposite to it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Many residents are against the plan to build on the park.
example_sentences: The team played against the champions and lost.
I have nothing against online lessons, but I prefer class.

confusables.difference: Both show disagreement. 'Against' is everyday and fine in speaking; 'opposed to' is more formal and suits Task 2 writing.

entry_json.definition: how old a person or thing is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Children start school at the age of five in my country.
example_sentences: At what age can you drive here?
People are living longer, so the average age is rising.
entry_json.avoid: Say "I am twenty" or "I am twenty years old", never "I have twenty years".

entry_json.definition: before now
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I moved to this city three years ago.
example_sentences: We met a long time ago.
The factory closed ten years ago.

confusables.difference: Ago counts back from now and follows the time: two years ago. Before counts back from a point in the past and comes after it too, but needs that point: two years before the war.

entry_json.avoid: 'Ago' goes with the past simple, never the present perfect. "I have seen him two days ago" is wrong.

entry_json.definition: to think the same as someone else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I agree that public transport should be cheaper.
example_sentences: Do you agree with this statement?
We agreed to meet outside the library.
entry_json.avoid: Agree is a verb on its own: "I agree", not "I am agree". You agree WITH a person and agree TO a plan.

entry_json.definition: a sound people make to show they now understand, or that they feel surprise or pity
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Ah, now I see what the question is asking.
example_sentences: Ah, that explains why the bus was late.
Ah, I'm sorry to hear that.
entry_json.avoid: This belongs in speech only. Never write it in an IELTS essay.

entry_json.definition: the gas all around us that we breathe
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The air in my home city is much cleaner than it was ten years ago.
example_sentences: Cyclists breathe in dirty air on busy roads.
I opened the window to let some fresh air in.
entry_json.avoid: Air is uncountable: not "airs".

entry_json.definition: a company that carries people and things by plane
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The airline lost my bag on the way to the conference.
example_sentences: Budget airlines have made flying much cheaper.
The airline offers three flights a day to Dubai.

entry_json.definition: a place where planes land and take off, with buildings for passengers
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The airport is forty minutes from the city by train.
example_sentences: I got to the airport two hours early.
A second airport would bring jobs but also noise.

entry_json.definition: living, not dead
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My great-grandmother is still alive and nearly a hundred.
example_sentences: The fish were still alive in the tank.
Traditional music is very much alive in the villages.

confusables.difference: 'Alive' comes after the verb: he is alive. 'Living' can come before a noun: a living language. We do not say "an alive man".

entry_json.avoid: Never put 'alive' before a noun.

entry_json.definition: the whole of something, or every one of a group
entry_json.own_context_sentence: All the students in my group passed the first test.
example_sentences: I spent all day in the library.
All of my friends use the same app.
entry_json.avoid: Before 'the', 'my' or 'these' you may use 'all' or 'all of': all the students, all of the students. Before a pronoun you need 'of': all of us.

entry_json.definition: to let someone do something, or to say that it is possible
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My university allows students to take one year out.
example_sentences: Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.
Flexible hours allow parents to collect their children.

confusables.difference: They mean the same, but the grammar differs. 'Let' takes no 'to': let me go. 'Allow' needs 'to': allow me to go. 'Let' is more spoken.

entry_json.avoid: Say "allow someone to do something". Not "allow to do" with no person.

entry_json.definition: very nearly, but not completely
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Almost half of my class travel to college by bus.
example_sentences: I have almost finished the report.
It took almost three hours to get there.

confusables.difference: In most sentences they are the same. Only 'almost' can be used with 'no', 'nobody' or 'never': almost never, but not 'nearly never'.

entry_json.avoid: Say "almost all of the students" or "almost every student", not "almost of the students".

entry_json.definition: from one end of something long towards the other, or in a line beside it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We walked along the river until we reached the market.
example_sentences: There are new cycle lanes along the main road.
Shops have opened all along the seafront.

confusables.difference: These look similar but are unrelated. Along is a direction; alone means with nobody else.

entry_json.definition: before now, or sooner than expected
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I had already booked my test before the fee went up.
example_sentences: She has already sent the application.
It is only ten o'clock and I am already tired.

confusables.difference: Already is for things that have happened, usually in a positive sentence. Yet is for things that have not happened, in questions and negatives: Have you finished yet? I haven't finished yet.
Still means something continues: I am still waiting. Already means it is finished: I have already waited.

entry_json.definition: in addition; as well
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course is cheap, and it is also close to my home.
example_sentences: She speaks French and also some Arabic.
Cycling saves money. It also keeps you fit.

confusables.difference: They mean the same, but 'also' goes in the middle of the sentence and 'too' goes at the end: I also went / I went too.

entry_json.avoid: Put 'also' before the main verb but after 'be': she also works, she is also busy.

entry_json.definition: another thing you could choose instead
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Cycling is a cheap alternative to driving in a crowded city.
example_sentences: Is there an alternative to raising the fees?
Solar power is a clean alternative to coal.
entry_json.avoid: Say "an alternative TO something", not "an alternative of".

entry_json.definition: used to join two ideas when the second one is surprising after the first
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Although the course was expensive, it was worth every penny.
example_sentences: Although I studied hard, I did not get the score I wanted.
The city is busy, although it is quiet at weekends.

confusables.difference: Both show contrast, but the grammar differs. 'Although' joins two clauses in one sentence. 'However' starts a new sentence and takes a comma: It was expensive. However, it was worth it.
'Although' is followed by a subject and verb; 'despite' is followed by a noun or -ing: although it rained / despite the rain.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use 'but' in the same sentence. "Although it was late, but I stayed" is wrong; drop the 'but'.

entry_json.definition: every time, or all the time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I always check my answers before the time is up.
example_sentences: The train is always crowded at eight in the morning.
She has always wanted to work in medicine.
entry_json.avoid: 'Always' goes before the main verb but after 'be': I always walk; I am always late.

entry_json.definition: very surprising and very good
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The view from the top of the hill was amazing.
example_sentences: She made amazing progress in six months.
It is amazing how quickly children pick up a language.

confusables.difference: 'Amazing' describes the thing that causes the feeling; 'amazed' describes the person who has it. The view was amazing, so I was amazed.

entry_json.avoid: 'Amazing' is strong and informal. In Task 2 writing, prefer 'remarkable' or 'impressive'.

entry_json.definition: in the middle of a group of people or things
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Cycling is popular among students who live near campus.
example_sentences: The book is among the most borrowed in the library.
Stress is common among first-year students.

confusables.difference: Use 'between' for two things, or for separate things you can name: between London and Paris. Use 'among' for a group you do not count: among the trees, among students.

entry_json.definition: how much of something there is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The amount of plastic in the sea has risen sharply.
example_sentences: A small amount of exercise each day makes a difference.
Students spend a huge amount of time online.

confusables.difference: Use 'amount' with things you cannot count: the amount of water, of time, of money. Use 'number' with things you can count: the number of cars, of students.

entry_json.avoid: Never "the amount of people". People can be counted, so use 'the number of people'.

entry_json.definition: belonging to a time very long ago
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city is famous for its ancient walls.
example_sentences: We visited an ancient temple in the north of the country.
Ancient Rome had a system of public baths.

confusables.difference: 'Ancient' means thousands of years old, or from a lost world. A phone from 2010 is old, not ancient — except as a joke.

entry_json.definition: used to join two words or two ideas together
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I study in the morning and work in the afternoon.
example_sentences: We visited the museum and the old market.
It was cold and wet all week.
entry_json.avoid: In writing, do not start every sentence with 'and'. Use 'in addition' or 'moreover' instead.

entry_json.definition: any person; it does not matter who

entry_json.definition: a small program you use on a phone or tablet

entry_json.definition: the soldiers who fight for a country on land

entry_json.definition: to plan or organise something so that it will happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I arranged to meet my tutor before the deadline.

entry_json.definition: painting, drawing and other work people make to be looked at

entry_json.definition: a piece of writing in a newspaper, a magazine or on a website
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I read an article about air quality in my home city.

entry_json.definition: a person who makes paintings, drawings or other works of art

entry_json.own_context_sentence: I asked the examiner to repeat the question.

entry_json.definition: sleeping

entry_json.avoid: 'Asleep' never goes before a noun. Say "the sleeping child", not "the asleep child".

entry_json.definition: a person whose job is to help someone else at work

entry_json.definition: to go to an event or a class

entry_json.definition: a young person who is not yet an adult

entry_json.definition: a long thin piece of potato cooked in hot oil

entry_json.definition: a sweet brown food made from cocoa beans
