entry_json.avoid: In Task 1 the chart 'illustrates' or 'shows' the data; it does not 'illustrate about' it.

entry_json.definition: a picture in a book or article, or an example that makes something clearer
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The floods are a stark illustration of what unplanned building can cost.
example_sentences: The textbook uses illustrations rather than photographs throughout.
By way of illustration, consider the case of a student with no internet at home.

contexts.text: The floods are a stark illustration of what unplanned building can cost.
The textbook uses illustrations rather than photographs throughout.
The children's books I loved all had beautiful illustrations.

confusables.difference: Example is the everyday word and is always safe. Illustration suggests the example does the extra work of making an abstract point visible.
A picture is any image. An illustration is drawn or made specifically to accompany a text.

entry_json.avoid: The preposition is 'an illustration of', never 'an illustration for' when you mean an example.

entry_json.definition: existing only in the mind, not real
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Young children often invent imaginary friends and talk to them for hours.
example_sentences: The line on the map marks an imaginary boundary, not a physical one.
Much of what we worry about before an exam turns out to be imaginary.

contexts.text: Young children often invent imaginary friends and talk to them for hours.
The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth.
As a child I had a whole imaginary world in the back garden.

confusables.difference: Imaginative is a compliment about a person or a piece of work: full of new ideas. Imaginary means the thing does not exist. Do not call a creative student 'imaginary'.
Fictional means invented for a story. Imaginary means invented in someone's mind, whether or not it appears in a book.

entry_json.avoid: 'Imaginary' cannot describe a person's ability. For that, use 'imaginative'.

entry_json.definition: the ability to form pictures and ideas in your mind, especially of things you have not seen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Reading fiction as a child does more for the imagination than any lesson.
example_sentences: The design shows real imagination given the tiny budget.
It takes little imagination to see where this policy leads.

contexts.text: Reading fiction as a child does more for the imagination than any lesson.
My little sister has an amazing imagination.
The exhibition captured the public imagination in a way nobody predicted.

confusables.difference: Creativity is producing something new. Imagination is the mental picturing that comes before it. You can have imagination without making anything.
Imagination is the noun for the ability; imaginary is the adjective for something unreal.

entry_json.avoid: Usually uncountable. 'Use your imagination' is right; 'use your imaginations' sounds odd even to a group.

entry_json.definition: happening or done at once, without delay; also nearest in space or relationship
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The immediate effect of the ban was a sharp drop in traffic.
example_sentences: The scheme brought no immediate benefit, though it paid off later.
Only immediate family were allowed into the ceremony.

contexts.text: The immediate effect of the ban was a sharp drop in traffic.
Only immediate family were allowed into the ceremony.
There was no immediate answer, so I sent a second email.

confusables.difference: Instant stresses that no time at all passes and often describes products ('instant coffee'). Immediate describes actions and consequences that follow at once.
Urgent says something must be done soon. Immediate says it happened or will happen without delay. A problem can be urgent but get no immediate response.

entry_json.avoid: The adverb is 'immediately'. Do not write 'he responded immediate'.

entry_json.definition: a person who comes to live permanently in a country that is not their own
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Immigrants make up nearly a fifth of the city's workforce.
example_sentences: Many immigrants arrive with qualifications that are not recognised here.
The second generation of immigrant families often speaks two languages fluently.

contexts.text: Immigrants make up nearly a fifth of the city's workforce.
Many immigrants arrive with qualifications that are not recognised here.
My grandparents were immigrants, so I grew up hearing two languages.

confusables.difference: The same person seen from the other side. You are an emigrant leaving your own country and an immigrant arriving in the new one.
A refugee has been forced to leave by war or persecution and has legal protection. An immigrant usually moves by choice, often for work or family.

entry_json.avoid: Because it names people, choose it carefully: 'immigrant workers' is neutral, but avoid 'illegal immigrant', which many readers find dehumanising.

entry_json.definition: a powerful effect that something has on a situation, a person or the environment
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The impact of the new railway on local businesses has been considerable.
example_sentences: Tourism has had a serious impact on the island's water supply.
The policy had little impact on the number of people cycling to work.

contexts.text: Tourism has had a serious impact on the island's water supply.
Moving to a new city had a big impact on my confidence.
The graph shows the impact of the fuel tax on consumption after 2015.

confusables.difference: Effect is neutral and covers any result. Impact suggests the result was strong and worth noticing, so it overstates a small change.
Influence works gradually and shapes how something develops. Impact lands, often at one moment, and is usually measurable.

entry_json.avoid: The preposition is 'impact on', not 'impact to'. Overusing 'impact' as a verb ('this impacts students') irritates many examiners; prefer 'affects'.

entry_json.definition: annoyed at having to wait, or wanting something to happen sooner than it can
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I get impatient in queues, which is a bad quality in a city this size.
example_sentences: Passengers grew impatient as the delay stretched into a second hour.
She was impatient to hear whether the application had succeeded.

contexts.text: I get impatient in queues, which is a bad quality in a city this size.
Passengers grew impatient as the delay stretched into a second hour.
Teachers should try not to sound impatient with students who are slow to answer.

confusables.difference: The direct opposite, and also a noun meaning someone receiving medical treatment. Context makes it clear, but the overlap surprises learners.
Annoyed is about something that has already irritated you. Impatient is specifically about waiting.

entry_json.avoid: Use 'impatient with' a person and 'impatient to' plus a verb. 'Impatient for' works only with a noun: 'impatient for news'.

entry_json.definition: to suggest something indirectly, without saying it openly; also, to make something a necessary consequence
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The figures imply that the scheme is working, though they do not prove it.
example_sentences: He never said the work was poor, but his tone implied it.
Rapid growth implies a rising demand for housing and schools.

contexts.text: The figures imply that the scheme is working, though they do not prove it.
He never said the work was poor, but his tone implied it.
A falling birth rate implies a smaller workforce within a generation.

confusables.difference: The speaker implies; the listener infers. If you write 'I implied from the graph', you have swapped them, which is a well-known error.

entry_json.avoid: Use 'imply' when the evidence is suggestive, not conclusive. If it is conclusive, 'show' or 'demonstrate' is more honest.

entry_json.definition: to buy goods from another country and bring them in to sell or use
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The country imports almost all of its wheat.
example_sentences: Britain imports far more food than it exports.
Cars imported from abroad face an additional tax.

contexts.text: The country imports almost all of its wheat.
Cars imported from abroad face an additional tax.
A lot of the fruit we buy is imported, which surprises people.

confusables.difference: Exact opposite direction: you import into your country and export out of it. Task 1 answers lose marks when these are swapped.

entry_json.avoid: Stress moves with the part of speech: the verb is imPORT, the noun is IMport.

entry_json.definition: the quality of being important; the value or significance something has
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Schools are finally recognising the importance of sleep for teenagers.
example_sentences: The report stresses the importance of early diagnosis.
People often underestimate the importance of small daily habits.

contexts.text: The report stresses the importance of early diagnosis.
I only realised the importance of practising speaking after my first test.
Governments attach growing importance to renewable energy.

confusables.difference: Significance is about meaning: what something tells us. Importance is about value: how much it matters. A small difference can have statistical significance without practical importance.

entry_json.avoid: 'Importance' is uncountable: write 'of great importance', not 'a great importance'.

entry_json.definition: to officially force a rule, tax or punishment on people, or to force your ideas on others
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city imposed a charge on vehicles entering the centre.
example_sentences: Heavy fines were imposed on companies that missed the deadline.
Parents should guide children rather than impose their own ambitions on them.

contexts.text: The city imposed a charge on vehicles entering the centre.
Heavy fines were imposed on companies that missed the deadline.
I don't think schools should impose a single way of learning on everyone.

entry_json.avoid: The pattern is 'impose something on somebody'. Do not write 'impose somebody to do something'.

entry_json.definition: to make someone feel admiration and respect for you or for something you have done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: What impressed me most was how patiently the staff explained everything.

The city's public transport impresses almost every visitor.

contexts.text: What impressed me most was how patiently the staff explained everything.
The candidate impressed the panel with her grasp of the figures.
Students often write to impress rather than to communicate.

entry_json.avoid: The pattern is 'impress somebody', not 'impress to somebody'. Use 'impress somebody with something'.

entry_json.definition: feeling admiration and respect for something you have seen or heard
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was genuinely impressed by how clean the city kept its streets.
example_sentences: The examiners were impressed with the range of vocabulary she used.
Visitors are usually impressed by the scale of the library.

contexts.text: I was genuinely impressed by how clean the city kept its streets.
The examiners were impressed with the range of vocabulary she used.
Employers are impressed by evidence of real experience, not by long lists of courses.

entry_json.avoid: Both 'impressed by' and 'impressed with' are correct. 'Impressed from' is not.

entry_json.definition: an idea or feeling you get about someone or something, especially at first
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My first impression of the university was that everyone seemed relaxed.
example_sentences: The photographs give a misleading impression of how big the flat is.
Candidates have about thirty seconds to make a good impression.

contexts.text: My first impression of the university was that everyone seemed relaxed.
The photographs give a misleading impression of how big the flat is.
Advertising works by creating an impression rather than by presenting evidence.

confusables.difference: An opinion is a considered judgement you could defend. An impression is a quick feeling that may not survive closer contact.

entry_json.definition: so good, large or skilful that people admire it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The city's recycling rate is impressive by any standard.
example_sentences: She gave an impressive presentation with almost no notes.
The improvement in reading scores over five years is impressive.

contexts.text: The city's recycling rate is impressive by any standard.
The old railway station is the most impressive building in my town.
The improvement in reading scores over five years is impressive.

confusables.difference: The thing is impressive; the person is impressed. Keep the direction straight.

entry_json.avoid: 'Impressive' is a judgement, not a measurement. In Task 1 report the figure first, then call it impressive if you must.

entry_json.definition: the fact of getting better, or a change that makes something better
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There has been a marked improvement in air quality since the ban.
example_sentences: Small improvements to the timetable made a real difference to commuters.
The latest figures show no improvement on last year.

contexts.text: There has been a marked improvement in air quality since the ban.
My writing showed a big improvement once I started reading more.
Small improvements to the timetable made a real difference to commuters.

confusables.difference: Development is growth into something more advanced or complete. Improvement is simply becoming better at what it already was.
Progress is uncountable and describes movement towards a goal. Improvement can be counted and measured against a previous state.

entry_json.avoid: Use 'an improvement in' a quality and 'an improvement on' a previous figure. 'Improvement of' is usually wrong.

entry_json.definition: a unit of length equal to 2.54 centimetres, still widely used in Britain and the United States
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The screen measures fifteen inches from corner to corner.
example_sentences: Rainfall was two inches above average for the month.
British recipes from the 1970s still give sizes in inches.

contexts.text: The screen measures fifteen inches from corner to corner.
British recipes from the 1970s still give sizes in inches.
Rainfall was two inches above average for the month.

confusables.difference: The metric equivalent, and the standard in academic writing everywhere. One inch is 2.54 centimetres.
Twelve inches make one foot. Heights are usually given in feet and inches together in Britain.

entry_json.avoid: Use metric units in Task 1 unless the chart itself uses inches. Mixing systems in one answer looks careless.

entry_json.definition: something that happens, especially something unusual, unpleasant or involving the police
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A single incident on the platform closed the whole line for an hour.
example_sentences: Staff must record every incident, however minor it seems.
There were no serious incidents during the festival.

contexts.text: A single incident on the platform closed the whole line for an hour.
Staff must record every incident, however minor it seems.
There was one incident on the trip that I still laugh about.

confusables.difference: An accident is unintended and usually causes harm. An incident may be deliberate, and the word is deliberately neutral about blame.
An event is anything that happens, including happy occasions. Incident implies something out of the ordinary, and often something bad.

entry_json.avoid: 'Incident' is formal and slightly official. In casual speech, 'something happened' is more natural.

entry_json.definition: the money a person or organisation receives regularly, from work, investments or benefits
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Households on a low income spend a far larger share of it on food.
example_sentences: Average income rose steadily throughout the period shown.
Tourism provides a significant share of the island's income.

contexts.text: Households on a low income spend a far larger share of it on food.
Average income rose steadily throughout the period shown.
My part-time job was my only income while I was studying.

confusables.difference: A salary is the fixed amount an employer pays you. Income is everything coming in, including a salary, rent, interest and benefits.

entry_json.definition: more and more over time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Employers are increasingly willing to accept fully remote staff.
example_sentences: Cities are increasingly dependent on a small number of food suppliers.
It is becoming increasingly difficult to find affordable rented housing.

contexts.text: Employers are increasingly willing to accept fully remote staff.
It is becoming increasingly difficult to find affordable rented housing.
Online shopping is increasingly popular with older people too.

confusables.difference: More compares two states. Increasingly describes a continuing trend, so it needs a process, not a single comparison.

entry_json.definition: extremely; also, in a way that is hard to believe
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The library gets incredibly busy in the last week of term.
example_sentences: It was incredibly kind of them to collect us from the airport.
Housing here has become incredibly expensive in a very short time.

contexts.text: The library gets incredibly busy in the last week of term.
It was incredibly kind of them to collect us from the airport.
Housing here has become incredibly expensive in a very short time.

confusables.difference: Extremely is the neutral choice and works in essays. Incredibly is conversational and slightly exaggerated.
The adjective goes before a noun ('an incredible view'); the adverb goes before an adjective ('incredibly beautiful').

entry_json.avoid: Avoid 'incredibly' in Task 2. 'Extremely', 'considerably' or 'markedly' carry the same force without the informality.

entry_json.definition: used to emphasise a statement, or to add information that strengthens what was just said
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The scheme was successful; indeed, it exceeded every target set for it.
example_sentences: Thank you very much indeed for arranging the visit.
Few students attended, and indeed some classes were cancelled entirely.

contexts.text: The scheme was successful; indeed, it exceeded every target set for it.
Thank you very much indeed for arranging the visit.
Few students attended, and indeed some classes were cancelled entirely.

confusables.difference: In fact often corrects or contrasts with what came before. Indeed agrees with it and pushes it further.
Actually is spoken and usually signals a correction. Indeed is more formal and confirms.

entry_json.avoid: As an answer on its own, 'Indeed.' sounds formal or slightly cold. 'Yes, absolutely' is friendlier in Speaking.

entry_json.definition: to show that something is probably true, or to point something out
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The figures indicate a steady fall in car ownership among under-thirties.
example_sentences: Early results indicate that the treatment is safe.
A red light indicates that the machine is still running.

contexts.text: The figures indicate a steady fall in car ownership among under-thirties.
Early results indicate that the treatment is safe.
He indicated the seat next to him without saying anything.

confusables.difference: Show is stronger and claims the evidence is clear. Indicate hedges: the evidence points that way without settling it.
Suggest is even more cautious than indicate. Order of confidence: prove, show, indicate, suggest.

entry_json.avoid: In Task 1, 'the chart indicates' is fine, but do not overuse it; vary with 'shows', 'reveals' and 'illustrates'.

entry_json.definition: not going in a straight line, or not caused immediately or openly by something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The indirect effects of the closure were felt across the whole town.
example_sentences: We took an indirect route because the main road was flooded.
The criticism was indirect but everyone in the room understood it.

contexts.text: The indirect effects of the closure were felt across the whole town.
We took an indirect route because the main road was flooded.
English speakers often make requests in an indirect way to sound polite.

confusables.difference: The opposite. Note that 'direct' can be a compliment about honesty in some cultures and a criticism in others.
Indirect describes the route by which something arrives or is said. Unclear says it cannot be understood. An indirect request can be perfectly clear.

entry_json.avoid: The adverb is 'indirectly'. Do not write 'he criticised her indirect'.

entry_json.definition: situated, done or used inside a building
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The town needs an indoor sports centre for the winter months.
example_sentences: Indoor air quality is often worse than people assume.
The school has an indoor pool that the public can use in the evenings.

contexts.text: The town needs an indoor sports centre for the winter months.
Indoor air quality is often worse than people assume.
I prefer indoor activities in winter and outdoor ones in summer.

confusables.difference: Indoor is an adjective and goes before a noun: 'an indoor market'. Indoors is an adverb and goes after a verb: 'we stayed indoors'.
Inside can be a preposition, adverb or noun. Indoor only ever modifies a noun.

entry_json.avoid: Never write 'we stayed indoor'. That needs the adverb 'indoors'.

entry_json.definition: inside a building, rather than outside
entry_json.own_context_sentence: People spend far more time indoors than they did a generation ago.
example_sentences: We had planned a picnic, but the rain drove us indoors.
Children who stay indoors all day get very little natural light.

contexts.text: People spend far more time indoors than they did a generation ago.
We had planned a picnic, but the rain drove us indoors.
Children who stay indoors all day get very little natural light.

confusables.difference: Indoors is the adverb; indoor is the adjective. 'An indoors pool' is wrong, as is 'we stayed indoor'.
Inside is more general and can refer to the inside of anything, including a bag or a car. Indoors always means inside a building.

entry_json.avoid: 'Indoors' always ends in -s and never goes before a noun.

entry_json.definition: connected with factories and the production of goods on a large scale
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The industrial area east of the river has been converted into flats.
example_sentences: Industrial emissions account for a large share of the country's carbon output.
Many former industrial towns have struggled to find a new role.

contexts.text: Industrial emissions account for a large share of the country's carbon output.
